Formulation:
- Predisposing: Chronic medical condition (SLE) and immunosuppression (methotrexate) may increase vulnerability to health-related anxiety.
- Precipitating: Sudden alarming physical symptoms (hemoptysis, pleuritic pain, dyspnea) triggered fears of lung cancer.
- Perpetuating: Uncertainty pending in-person assessment; online/health-related catastrophic thoughts; living alone may limit immediate reassurance (extent not recorded).
- Protective: Rapid help-seeking; rapport with GP; planned medical evaluation which may reduce uncertainty.

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem: Health-related anxiety related to acute respiratory symptoms and fear of cancer
- Patient Goal(s):
  - Reduce anxiety while awaiting medical evaluation
  - Understand medical plan and expected next steps
  - Maintain function at work and home
- Clinical Goal(s):
  - Provide validation and brief psychoeducation about anxiety in the context of medical symptoms
  - Safety-net and develop interim coping plan while medical workup proceeds
  - Reassess anxiety severity after acute medical issues are addressed; consider screening (e.g., GAD-7) if symptoms persist
- Actions (Patient):
  - Follow medical assessment plan (same-day in-person review)
  - Use brief coping strategies: paced breathing (e.g., 4-6 breaths/min), scheduled worry time, limit excessive online searching about cancer, maintain routine and light activity as tolerated
  - Identify one supportive contact to update and seek reassurance from (if available)
  - Return/seek urgent care if anxiety escalates to panic, or if new/worsening medical red flags occur (per GP guidance)
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Reinforce that acute presentation is more consistent with infection per clinical discussion; clarify medical next steps and timelines
  - Provide written/portal-based safety-netting advice and reputable resources on health anxiety (if available)
  - Arrange brief follow-up check-in after in-person assessment to review anxiety symptoms
  - If persistent significant anxiety after medical stabilization, consider referral for brief CBT-based intervention and administer standardized screening (e.g., GAD-7); consider collaborative care

Secondary Problem (if applicable): Fatigue with functional impact (likely medical; monitor mental health impact)
- Patient Goal(s):
  - Maintain daily routines and pacing while under medical evaluation
- Clinical Goal(s):
  - Monitor for depressive or anxiety symptoms if fatigue persists after medical treatment
- Actions (Patient):
  - Activity pacing; prioritize sleep hygiene; note energy patterns
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Reassess mood/anxiety if fatigue persists beyond medical recovery; consider PHQ-9 screening if indicated
